1.title: The vision of Isaiah
1.text: Isaiah prophesied in Judah under four kings: Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah.

1.question: How does Isaiah describe the rebellious people's condition?
options: The whole head strong and the whole heart glad
The whole head sick and the whole heart faint
The whole body healthy and the whole spirit strong
Whole from head to foot, without blemish

1.question: To whom does the Lord liken the rulers and people of Judah?
options: To the kings of Israel and the chosen people of Judah
To the rulers of Sodom and people of Gomorrah
To the priests of Babylon and the people of the Chaldeans
To the Philistines and the rebellious Ammonites

1.question: Why does the Lord hide His eyes and not hear their prayers?
options: Their lips speak lies and vanity
Their hands are full of blood
Their hearts are far from the Lord

1.question: According to 1:18, though your sins be as scarlet, they shall become?
What will the city be called after it is purified?
options: The city of sin, the city of destruction and wrath
The city of righteousness, the faithful city
The city of wrath, the city that was destroyed
The city of false and worthless idols

1.question: According to 1:27, with what shall Zion be redeemed?

2.title: The Lord's mountain
2.text: The last-days vision (2:2-4) foretells peace among nations and the law going forth from Zion.

2.question: Into what will the nations beat their swords?
Besides silver and gold, with what was the land of Judah full?
Against whom will the day of the Lord of hosts be?
options: Everyone humble and meek of heart

2.question: What is the counsel of 2:22?
options: Trust fully in strong armies and mighty horses of war
Cease from man, whose breath is in his nostrils
Seek riches and hidden treasures deep in the earth
Worship the idols of neighboring nations

3.title: Leadership removed
3.text: God takes away Jerusalem's stays and gives children to rule — a sign of social collapse.

3.question: Whom does the Lord say He will give as princes to Jerusalem?
What is to be said to the righteous?
options: That he shall suffer greatly indeed
That it shall be well with him
That he shall surely be punished
That he will flee far away

3.question: Of what does the Lord accuse the elders and princes?
options: Of praying far too little of the time
Of grinding the faces of the poor
Of building many temples and altars

3.question: The chapter describes the removal of what from the daughters of Zion?
What will happen to Zion's gates?
options: They will be rebuilt in glory
They will stand open day and night

4.title: The Branch of the Lord
4.text: Amid judgment, hope arises: the 'Branch' and the holy remnant of Zion.

4.question: According to 4:2, the Branch of the Lord shall be?

5.title: The song of the vineyard
5.text: God tended the vineyard, but it yielded wild grapes — a figure of Israel and its injustice.

5.question: What did the vineyard yield instead of good grapes?
According to 5:7, what is the vineyard of the Lord of hosts?
To whom is the woe of those who rise early (5:11)?
options: Those who oppress the orphans of the land
Those who mock the true prophets

5.question: According to 5:20, against whom is the woe?
options: Those who call evil good, and good evil
Those who oppress the widows and the orphans of the land
Those who raise up altars to foreign idols
Those who despise the poor of the land

5.question: What refrain marks the Lord's anger in this chapter?
options: His hand is stretched out still
His anger has turned away completely
His glory has filled all the earth
His people will soon be restored

5.question: To whom will the Lord hiss, lifting an ensign (5:26)?
options: To the king of Assyria himself

6.title: Holy, Holy, Holy
6.text: In the year Uzziah died, Isaiah sees the Lord on the throne and is commissioned.

6.question: What does Isaiah say when he sees the Lord?
options: Blessed art thou, Lord, for I see thy glory
Woe is me, I am undone, a man of unclean lips
I will not fear, for I am ready to serve
Who art thou, appearing in this temple?

6.question: How does Isaiah answer 'Whom shall I send?'
options: I am not worthy, choose another
Send my brother in my place
I am not ready yet, O Lord

6.question: To what is the tenth that remains compared (6:13)?
options: To the felled and dried stump

7.title: The sign of Immanuel
7.text: Isaiah urges King Ahaz to believe God before the threat of Syria and Israel.

7.question: How does God call the two enemy kings Ahaz feared?
According to 7:9, if you will not believe?
options: You will win the great battle

7.question: What sign will the Lord Himself give the house of David?
options: A great famine will ravage the land until the end of days
A virgin shall conceive and bear a son, Immanuel
A foreign army will besiege the city of Jerusalem
A new covenant will be made with all the house of Israel

7.question: Before the child knows to choose good, the land of the two kings shall be?
With what will the Lord 'shave' the head (7:20)?
options: With a sword forged in the lands of Egypt
With a hired razor (the king of Assyria)
With an ancient axe brought from Babylon
With stones carried from the Jordan River

8.title: Maher-shalal-hash-baz
8.text: The name of Isaiah's son means 'speed to the spoil' — a sign of the imminent fall of Damascus and Samaria.

8.question: What name is given to the son, a sign of the speed of the spoil?
According to 8:8, the flood (Assyria) will reach how far?
According to 8:10, why will the enemies' counsel not stand?
Instead of consulting mediums and the dead, to what should one turn (8:20)?
options: To the law and to the testimony
To the signs of heaven and the stars
To the ancient traditions of the fathers

9.title: Unto us a child is born
9.text: Isaiah 9:6 proclaims the Messiah's names, read at Christmas worldwide.

9.question: Which of these is one of the names of the child born (9:6)?
According to 9:7, upon whose throne will His kingdom be established?
How are the leaders of this people described (9:16)?
What refrain is repeated about the Lord's anger?
options: His hand is stretched out still
His anger has turned away forever
The Lord will pity the orphans
All the people will repent fully

10.title: The rod of mine anger
10.text: God uses Assyria to punish, but will judge its arrogance.

10.question: What does the Lord call Assyria in 10:5?
What does Assyria boast of in 10:9?
options: Having subdued nations like Edom and Ammon by force
Having conquered cities like Calno and Carchemish
Possessing riches greater than the king of Judah's
Its own great wisdom and military power

10.question: How does Assyria boast of gathering the nations' riches?
options: Like one gathering hidden treasures in caves
Like one gathering abandoned eggs in a nest
Like one gathering scattered flocks in the fields
Like one gathering ripe fruit in summer

10.question: Upon whom will Israel's remnant lean again (10:20)?
options: In the power of their own weapons
The Lord, the Holy One of Israel
In the gods of neighboring nations

10.question: What does the Lord tell His people about Assyria (10:24)?
options: To flee quickly to the far distant mountains
Not to fear, for His anger will soon cease
To prepare themselves for a long and hard battle
To trust only in their own weapons

10.question: The chapter describes the enemy's advance passing cities like?
options: Tyre, Sidon, and the land of Gaza
Bethel, Shiloh, and the city of Hebron

10.question: According to 10:34, what will fall by a mighty one?

11.title: The rod of Jesse
11.text: Messianic prophecy: the Branch of David's line and the kingdom of peace.

11.question: According to 11:1, from where will the rod and Branch come?
According to 11:6, who will dwell with the lamb?
What will the Lord do for the dispersed of Israel and Judah (11:12)?
options: Scatter them even further among all the distant nations of the earth
Set up an ensign and gather them from the ends of the earth
Leave them forgotten forever in the lands of captivity
Send a prophet to warn them of the coming danger

12.title: Song of praise
12.text: A brief hymn of gratitude closes the first section of the book.

12.question: According to 12:3, from where shall water be drawn with joy?
options: The rivers of the promised land
The waters of the Red Sea

13.title: The burden of Babylon
13.text: Opens the series of oracles against the nations.

13.question: According to 13:10, what will happen to sun, moon, and stars?
options: Fall upon the earth like rain of fire
Move from their place and form a new sky
Shine with an intense red glow

13.question: According to 13:12, what will God make more precious than fine gold?
To what will Babylon be compared in its fall (13:19)?

14.title: The fall of the proud
14.text: The proverb against the king of Babylon and the lament over the 'morning star.'

14.question: What proverb will Israel take up against the king of Babylon?
options: 'The scepter of the tyrant is broken!'
'How is the mighty one brought down!'

14.question: According to 14:9, whom does hell rouse to meet the one who falls?
options: The fallen angels and the princes of darkness
The dead and the kings of nations
The giants and the forgotten kings of the earth
The evil spirits of all the earth

14.question: Who said 'I will ascend into heaven... I will be like the most High' and was cast down?
options: The king of Assyria, lord of the north and east
The morning star (son of the morning)
The prince of Philistia, guardian of the nations
The guardian angel who covered the sacred temple

14.question: Why will the seed of evildoers not be named (14:20)?
options: Because they worshiped foreign idols instead of the Lord
Because they destroyed their land and slew their people
Because they secretly allied with the enemies of Israel and Judah
Because they completely abandoned the Lord their God

14.question: What nation will the Lord break in His own land (14:25)?
What shall be answered to the nations' messengers (14:32)?
options: That Judah has surrendered to the enemy
That the Lord hath founded Zion
That the king of Assyria has prevailed

15.title: The burden of Moab
15.text: A lament for Moab's cities, laid waste by night.

15.question: Against what nation is this burden?
What will the Lord send upon those who escape from Moab (15:9)?

16.title: The throne in mercy
16.text: Amid Moab's judgment shines 16:5: a throne established in mercy.

16.question: According to 16:5, in what will the throne be established?
Within how many years will Moab's glory be brought to contempt (16:14)?

17.title: The burden of Damascus
17.text: Damascus, capital of Syria, shall cease to be a city.

17.question: According to 17:1, what will Damascus become?
According to 17:7, to whom will man look in that day?
options: To the foreign gods of ancient Damascus
To his Maker (the Holy One of Israel)
To the graven images of their own hands
To the sacred groves and idol poles

17.question: According to 17:14, what is the lot of those who spoil us?
options: In the morning they shall greatly rejoice and receive an eternal reward
At evening trouble; before morning they are not
At dawn they shall be exalted and shall reign forever in great honor
In the evening they receive rest and lasting peace

18.title: Beyond the rivers of Cush
18.text: A brief oracle on a nation that sends ambassadors; God watches in silence.

18.question: According to 18:7, where shall a present be brought to the Lord of hosts?

19.title: The burden of Egypt
19.text: Judgment on Egypt that ends in a vision of conversion.

19.question: How does the Lord come to Egypt (19:1)?
options: Mounted upon a chariot of burning fire
Descending from heaven with an army of angels
Walking upon the waters of the sea

19.question: According to 19:2, against whom will God set the Egyptians?
options: Against the children of Israel who once dwelt among them
Against the Egyptians themselves (city against city)
Against the combined great armies of Assyria and Babylon
Against the priests and the wise men of Zoan

19.question: What did the Lord mingle in the midst of Egypt (19:14)?
According to 19:20, what will God send to Egypt when they cry out?
options: An army of avenging angels sent to destroy the land
A Saviour and a great one (a Redeemer)
A plague of locusts and severe famine upon the people
A new foreign king to rule over them

19.question: How is Israel called in the final blessing (19:25)?

20.title: Naked and barefoot
20.text: Isaiah enacts a sign against trusting in Egypt and Ethiopia.

20.question: For how many years did Isaiah walk naked and barefoot as a sign (20:3)?

21.title: Babylon is fallen
21.text: A watchman keeps guard until he announces Babylon's fall.

21.question: In 21:2, who is called to lay siege?
What does the watchman finally announce (21:9)?
options: 'Flee all, for the enemy now comes!'

21.question: Against which region is the burden of 21:13?
According to 21:16, within a year the glory of Kedar will be?

22.title: The valley of vision
22.text: Jerusalem feasts before judgment; Shebna is deposed and Eliakim exalted.

22.question: About what place is the burden of 22:1?
In making the reservoir, to whom did the people not look (22:11)?
options: To the king who reigned in Jerusalem (Hezekiah)
To Him who made it (who fashioned it)
To the prophets who foretold the destruction
To the fortified walls of the city

22.question: What did the people say instead of weeping (22:13)?
options: 'Let us weep and fast, for the Lord will judge us'
'Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die'
'Let us flee to the mountains before all perishes'
'Let us rebuild the walls before the war'

22.question: Whom will the Lord call in Shebna's place (22:20)?
options: Hezekiah, son of Ahaz, the king
Isaiah, son of Amoz, the prophet
Urijah, the priest of the temple

22.question: What will be laid on Eliakim's shoulder (22:22)?
options: A sword with two sharp edges
The key of the house of David
A scepter of pure shining gold
A robe of fine linen cloth

23.title: The burden of Tyre
23.text: Tyre was the wealthy Phoenician port, 'the crowning city,' whose merchants were princes.

23.question: Against what city is this burden?
Who purposed it against Tyre, to stain its pride?
options: The king of Assyria, with his army

23.question: What people is mentioned in 23:13, whom Assyria founded for the wilderness?
For how many years will Tyre be forgotten (23:15)?

24.title: Isaiah's apocalypse
24.text: Chs. 24-27 describe a cosmic judgment upon the whole earth.

24.question: Why is the earth defiled (24:5)?
options: Because the people worshiped idols in the high places
Because they broke the everlasting covenant
Because the inhabitants oppressed the poor and the orphans
Because the priests had profaned the temple

24.question: According to 24:1, what does the Lord do to the earth?
What does 24:15 say to do to the Lord in the valleys and isles?
According to 24:20, the earth shall reel to and fro like?
What happens to the sun and moon when the Lord reigns in Zion (24:23)?
options: They shine brighter than ever before
They fall from the heavens to earth
They vanish forever from the sky

25.title: A song of praise
25.text: Gratitude for God's protection and the promise of victory over death.

25.question: According to 25:4, to whom was the Lord a strength?
options: Of kings and princes of the earth
To the poor and the needy

25.question: According to 25:8, what will the Lord do with death and tears?
options: Increase death and multiply human suffering greatly
Swallow up death in victory and wipe away tears
Ignore the tears and increase the sorrow of the people
Delay death for a few more years still

25.question: According to 25:6, what will the Lord make on this mountain for all peoples?

26.title: A song of trust
26.text: In Judah they sing of trust in the Lord, the everlasting rock, and the hope of resurrection.

26.question: According to 26:3, whom does the Lord keep in peace?
options: Him whose mind is stayed on Him
The rich who trust in their riches

26.question: According to 26:10, what does the wicked not learn, even when shown favor?
According to 26:13, what does the people remember, despite other lords?
What does Isaiah affirm about the dead in 26:19?
options: They shall remain dead forevermore in the dust
Thy dead men shall live (rise again)
They shall never rise from their tombs
They shall be erased from memory

27.title: The Lord's vineyard
27.text: God keeps His vineyard and gathers the scattered at the sound of a great trumpet.

27.question: What creature will the Lord punish with His sword (27:1)?
options: The wild bull from the mountains of the north
The giant eagle that flies over the sea
The great scorpion of the desert

27.question: According to 27:6, what will Jacob and Israel do?
options: Be scattered among all the nations of the earth
Take root and fill the world with fruit
Fall under the yoke of the foreign enemy
Return to ancient bondage in Egypt

27.question: According to 27:13, at the great trumpet, what will the scattered do?
options: Flee away to the distant mountains
Gather together to fight against Zion

28.title: Precept upon precept
28.text: Woe to the drunkards of Ephraim; instruction comes little by little, and God lays the corner stone in Zion.

28.question: The woe of 28:1 is to whose crown of pride?
According to 28:7, why do even the priest and prophet err?
options: Because of great wealth and pride

28.question: How does instruction come, according to 28:10?
options: Through voices coming from the sacred temple
Precept upon precept, line upon line
Through angels sent directly from heaven
Through dreams and visions in the night

28.question: What stone does the Lord lay in Zion as a foundation (28:16)?
options: A stone of severe judgment for the rebellious
A precious corner stone, a sure foundation
A stumbling stone and scandal for the unbelieving
A rough stone not yet hewn by hands

28.question: The parable of 28:24-29 is about whom, to show God's wisdom?
From whom does the plowman's wisdom come (28:29)?

29.title: Woe to Ariel
29.text: Ariel is Jerusalem, the city where David camped; it will be brought low and then restored.

29.question: What did the Lord pour out upon them (29:10)?
options: A rain of fire and brimstone
A strong wind from the desert

29.question: According to 29:13, how does this people honor God?
options: With fasts and sacrifices without any sincerity
With mouth and lips, but heart far away
With songs and feasts, but without true obedience
With rich but vain offerings before the Lord

29.question: In 29:16, the people's perversity is compared to what?
options: A mighty army that marches against Zion without any fear
The potter treated as the clay (the work denying its maker)
A storm that destroys everything without leaving any trace
A river that overflows and floods the whole city

29.question: According to 29:18, what will the deaf and blind do in that day?

30.title: Trusting in Egypt
30.text: Woe to the rebels who seek Egypt; but in quietness and confidence is strength.

30.question: To whom do the rebellious children go down for strength (30:2)?
What does the people ask of the prophets (30:10)?
According to 30:15, in confidence and quietness would be strength, but the people?
What voice will be heard behind them (30:21)?
options: 'Return in haste to the land of Egypt'
'This is the way, walk ye in it'

30.question: According to 30:26, how will the light of the sun be in that day?
According to 30:29, there will be a song as in the night when one?
According to 30:31, by the voice of the Lord, who shall be beaten down?

31.title: Egypt is man, not God
31.text: Trusting in Egypt's horses and chariots is vain; the Lord will defend Jerusalem.

31.question: Woe to those who go down to Egypt and trust in (31:1)?
According to 31:8, by what sword shall Assyria fall?
options: By the sword of the ancient Philistines
By the strength of allied armies

32.title: A King shall reign in righteousness
32.text: Vision of the righteous King and the peace that comes when the spirit is poured from on high.

32.question: According to 32:1, how shall the King reign?
Whom does Isaiah call to listen in 32:9?
options: The princes and counselors of the land
The women at ease and careless
The priests and elders of the temple
The mighty warriors of the city

32.question: According to 32:15, what will turn the wilderness into a fruitful field?
options: The abundant rain sent from heaven
The spirit poured from on high
The hard labor of the chosen people
The decree of the just king

32.question: According to 32:17, what shall be the work of righteousness?

33.title: The King in His beauty
33.text: Woe to the spoiler; the righteous shall dwell on high and see the King.

33.question: To whom is the woe of 33:1?
options: The people who rebelled against the Lord
The priest who deceived all the people of Zion

33.question: What does the Lord say He will do 'now' (33:10)?
options: Utterly destroy all the rebellious nations
Arise, be exalted, and lift Himself up
Hide Himself from His enemies for a season
Rest from all the work of creation

33.question: According to 33:15-16, who shall dwell on high, with sure bread and water?
options: The rich man who trusts in his riches
The warrior who trusts in his sword

33.question: According to 33:20, Zion is described as a tabernacle that?
options: Will be sold to the enemies

33.question: According to 33:24, the people who dwell there shall be?

34.title: The judgment of Edom
34.text: The Lord's sword descends on Edom; the land will lie desolate forever.

34.question: Upon what people will the Lord's sword descend for judgment (34:5)?
What birds will possess Edom's desolate land (34:11)?
options: Doves and turtledoves of the fields
Eagles and falcons of the open heavens

34.question: Where should one seek and read that none of this shall fail (34:16)?
options: In the ancient writings of the prophets
In the book of the Lord
In the stars of the firmament
In the chronicles of the kings

35.title: The desert shall blossom
35.text: A chapter of hope: healing, joy, and the holy way back to Zion.

35.question: According to 35:1, what will the wilderness do?
options: Dry up completely and bear no more fruit
Be glad and blossom as the rose
Tremble in fear before the wrath of the Lord
Burn with everlasting flames and smoke

35.question: What will the highway of 35:8 be called?
options: The broad road of the city

36.title: Rabshakeh defies Jerusalem
36.text: The Assyrian envoy mocks Judah's trust in God and in Egypt.

36.question: Who came up against Judah and sent Rabshakeh (36:1-2)?
options: Tirhakah, king of the land of Ethiopia

36.question: In what 'broken reed' does Rabshakeh say Judah trusts (36:6)?
In what language did Rabshakeh cry out loudly (36:13)?
options: Syrian, the language of the court

36.question: What does Rabshakeh mock, saying the gods of the nations could not do (36:18)?
options: Prevent the fall of their cities before other kings
Deliver their lands from the king of Assyria
Heal the wounds of war for their worshipers
Defeat the armies of the king of Assyria

36.question: Why did the people not answer Rabshakeh (36:21)?
options: Because they feared Rabshakeh would strike them with the sword
The king had commanded: answer him not
Because Isaiah had forbidden any answer
Because they were astonished at his words

37.title: Hezekiah's prayer
37.text: Hezekiah prays, and the angel of the Lord delivers Jerusalem miraculously.

37.question: What did Hezekiah do on hearing Rabshakeh's words (37:1)?
options: Gathered his army and went out to meet the king of Assyria in battle
Rent his clothes, put on sackcloth, and went into the house of the Lord
Sent gifts and riches to appease the wrath of the Assyrian king
Summoned the priests to offer sacrifices in the temple

37.question: What does Sennacherib's letter try to make Hezekiah believe (37:10)?
options: That he should ally with Egypt against Assyria
That his God would not deliver Jerusalem
That the Lord had already abandoned his people forever
That Isaiah was a false prophet

37.question: In his prayer, Hezekiah declares who alone is God of all kingdoms (37:16)?
How does Isaiah say the daughter of Zion reacts to the Assyrian king (37:22)?
options: Receives him with great honors and many gifts
Despises him and laughs him to scorn
Hails him as a mighty deliverer and hero
Bows down low before him in fear

37.question: What did Sennacherib boast of, defying the Lord (37:24)?
options: Conquering single-handedly all the kingdoms of the whole earth
Climbing the mountains and cutting Lebanon's cedars
Destroying all the temples of the foreign gods and idols
Defeating the entire Egyptian army single-handedly

37.question: The Lord promises the Assyrian king will not do what to the city (37:33)?
options: Will not leave one stone upon another in it
Will not enter it nor shoot an arrow
Will not allow his armies to besiege it

37.question: How many did the angel of the Lord smite in the Assyrian camp (37:36)?
options: One hundred and twenty-five thousand men

38.title: Fifteen more years
38.text: Hezekiah falls mortally ill, prays, and the Lord prolongs his life.

38.question: How many years did the Lord add to Hezekiah's life (38:5)?
What sign did the Lord give, on the sundial (degrees) of Ahaz (38:8)?
options: The sun stood still for an entire day
The shadow went back ten degrees
The shadow moved forward twenty degrees

38.question: What did the Lord cast behind His back (38:17)?
options: The whole disease consuming him within

38.question: What poultice did Isaiah order laid on the boil (38:21)?

39.title: The envoys of Babylon
39.text: Hezekiah shows his treasures, and Isaiah foretells the Babylonian exile.

39.question: What did Hezekiah show the messengers of Babylon (39:2)?
options: Only the gifts they had given
The letters sent by Babylon's king

39.question: Where does Isaiah prophesy all will be carried (39:6)?

40.title: Comfort ye my people
40.text: Opens the second part of Isaiah, of comfort and redemption.

40.question: How does chapter 40 begin?
options: 'Arise, shine, for thy light is come'
'Cry out, cry out against my people'
'Hear the word of the Lord, O sons'

40.question: What does the voice in the wilderness cry (40:3)?
options: 'Lift up a banner upon the mountain'
'Prepare ye the way of the Lord'

40.question: Before God, the nations are as (40:15)?
options: As the sand of the sea

40.question: According to 40:18, to whom can God be likened?
What will they that wait upon the Lord do (40:31)?
options: They will grow weary and faint like young men without strength
Renew their strength and mount up with wings as eagles
They will lose their strength and fall exhausted along the long path
They will fall from weariness and lose heart on the way

41.title: Fear not, I am with thee
41.text: God comforts Israel, His servant, and exposes the vanity of idols.

41.question: Who is the first and with the last, calling the generations (41:4)?
What does God say to Israel in 41:10?
options: 'Wait, for the time is not yet come'
'Fear not, for I am with thee'

41.question: How does God call Israel as He comforts it (41:14)?
What will God do in the wilderness (41:18)?
options: Send fire from heaven upon them
Raise walls around the whole earth

41.question: From where does God raise the one who will come (41:25)?
options: The south (the land of the Philistines)
The north (the rising of the sun)
The distant isles of the west

41.question: According to 41:29, what are the molten images?
options: Sacred and full of great power
Powerful enough to save the people

42.title: The song of the Servant
42.text: The first of the four 'Servant Songs,' read as prophecy of Christ.

42.question: What will the Servant not do to the bruised reed or smoking flax (42:3)?
options: Kindle the reed and burn the flax until it is gone
Break the reed or quench the flax
Throw away the reed and quench the flax for good
Hide the reed and the flax in the desert

42.question: For what did God give the Servant (42:6)?
options: To reign as king over all the nations of the whole earth
For a covenant of the people and a light to the gentiles
To conquer Babylon and set the whole people free by force
To judge the kings of the earth with great power

42.question: According to 42:8, to whom will the Lord not give His glory?
options: To no one; nor His praise to graven images
To the kings of the earth; nor His praise to idols of the nations
To the prophets; nor His praise to the priests of the temple
To the gentiles; nor His praise to the angels of heaven

42.question: According to 42:16, God will turn the darkness before the blind into?
How is the people described in 42:22?

43.title: I have redeemed thee
43.text: Promises of presence and forgiveness: God calls Israel by name.

43.question: According to 43:2, passing through the fire, the people shall not be?
How does God call Israel in 43:10?
For Israel's sake, against whom did God send enemies (43:14)?
What will God do anew (43:19)?
